claims.text: What the strip looks like QRS complexes 120 ms or wider.
claims.quote: Wide (≥ 120 ms): Bundle branch block, ventricular rhythm, hyperkalemia, sodium channel blocker toxicity, pre-excitation

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) QRS: ≥ 120 ms (> 120 ms is needed to call bundle branch block or a ventricular rhythm)
claims.quote: A QRS duration > 120 ms is required for the diagnosis of bundle branch block or ventricular rhythm

claims.text: P waves: a supraventricular rhythm conducted with aberrancy usually shows atrial activity before the QRS (P, flutter or fibrillatory waves)
claims.quote: In general, aberrant conduction of sinus rhythm and atrial rhythms (tachycardia, flutter, fibrillation) can usually be identified by the presence of preceding atrial activity (P waves, flutter waves, fibrillatory waves).

claims.text: P waves: none before the QRS in ventricular rhythms — and in aberrant junctional beats, which can look identical
claims.quote: However, aberrantly conducted junctional (AV nodal) complexes may appear identical to ventricular complexes as both produce broad QRS without any preceding atrial activity.

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Mechanism: ventricular origin (below the His bundle), or a supraventricular rhythm conducted with an intraventricular conduction defect or WPW pre-excitation
claims.quote: A wide QRS complex (≥ 0.12 seconds) indicates a ventricular origin (below the His bundle bifurcation), or a supraventricular rhythm conducted with an intraventricular conduction defect or with ventricular preexcitation in the Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

claims.text: Diagnoses: bundle branch block, ventricular rhythm, hyperkalemia, sodium channel blocker toxicity, pre-excitation
claims.quote: Wide (≥ 120 ms): Bundle branch block, ventricular rhythm, hyperkalemia, sodium channel blocker toxicity, pre-excitation

claims.text: Also ventricular pacing, hypothermia and rate-related aberrancy
claims.quote: Ventricular pacing Hypothermia Intermittent aberrancy (e.g. rate-related aberrancy)

claims.text: Tell the causes apart by pattern RBBB: RSR' in V1, deep slurred S waves in the lateral leads
claims.quote: Right bundle branch block produces an RSR’ pattern in V1 and deep slurred S waves in the lateral leads.

claims.text: LBBB: dominant S in V1; broad, notched R waves and no Q waves laterally
claims.quote: Left bundle branch block produces a dominant S wave in V1 with broad, notched R waves and absent Q waves in the lateral leads.

claims.text: Hyperkalemia: peaked T waves among other changes
claims.quote: Hyperkalaemia is associated with a range of abnormalities including peaked T waves

claims.text: Tricyclic poisoning: sinus tachycardia and a tall R' wave in aVR
claims.quote: Tricyclic poisoning is associated with sinus tachycardia and tall R’ wave in aVR

claims.text: WPW: short PR and delta waves
claims.quote: Wolff-Parkinson White syndrome is characterised by a short PR interval and delta waves

claims.text: Ventricular pacing: usually visible pacing spikes
claims.quote: Ventricular pacing will usually have visible pacing spikes

claims.text: Hypothermia: bradycardia, long QT, Osborn waves, shivering artifact
claims.quote: Hypothermia is associated with bradycardia, long QT, Osborn waves and shivering artefact

claims.text: Key trap A wide-complex tachycardia is VT until proven otherwise
claims.quote: Assuming a wide-complex tachycardia is SVT with aberrancy — it's VT until proven otherwise
claims.locator: 15. Quick Reference Summary, The Most Common Traps

notes.issue: "Otherwise those of the cause; treatment is directed at the cause" was unsupported (arrhythmia-treatment quote; nothing supports symptoms).
notes.resolution: Claim removed; preceding label renamed to Key trap.
